title: MG Road Bangalore Shopping Guide: What to Buy, Where to Eat, Where to Go After Dark
summary: Mg road bangalore shopping: covering malls, street shopping, restaurants, cafes, pubs, nightlife spots, how to reach by metro.
body_text: The stretch runs barely 2 km from Trinity Circle to Anil Kumble Circle, but it packs in luxury malls, craft beer, silk showrooms, 1980s pubs, rooftop lounges, and South Indian filter coffee all within walking distance of a single metro station. That density is exactly why any MG Road Bangalore shopping guide worth reading also covers what to eat and where to go after the shops close. This guide breaks down MG Road and its connecting streets (Brigade Road, Church Street, Lavelle Road) into three clear sections: where to shop and what to buy, where to eat from Rs 100 to Rs 3,000, and where to spend the evening. Practical details like metro exits, walking distances, and price ranges sit alongside every recommendation. MG Road Bangalore Shopping Guide: What to Buy, Where to Eat, Where to Go After Dark MG Road, originally called South Parade during British colonial rule, was renamed Mahatma Gandhi Road on 26 February 1948. It runs east to west through the heart of Bangalore’s Central Business District, connecting Trinity Circle on one end to Anil Kumble Circle on the other. The road itself is lined with retail stores, office buildings, banks, and restaurants on both sides, but what makes the area significant for visitors is the network of streets that branch off it. Brigade Road splits south from MG Road near the midpoint and runs down to Residency Road. Church Street runs parallel on the north side, roughly 750 metres long, packed with cafes, bookstores, pubs, and restaurants. Lavelle Road and Vittal Mallya Road connect on the south side, hosting Bangalore’s luxury hotel and fine dining cluster. Commercial Street sits about 1.5 km northeast, accessible on foot or by a short auto ride. Together, these streets form the single densest zone for shopping, eating, and nightlife in the city. The area holds Cubbon Park on its northern edge and Parade Ground as a colonial era landmark. The Purple Line of Namma Metro runs along this stretch with MG Road Metro Station and Trinity Metro Station providing direct access. That metro connectivity, combined with the concentration of activities within a 1.5 km radius, makes this the most walkable entertainment district in Bangalore. Shopping on MG Road: Malls, Showrooms and Street Finds The mg road bangalore shopping guide starts with understanding the three tiers of retail the area offers. You have large air-conditioned malls carrying international and national brands, standalone showrooms selling Karnataka specific products, and street vendors offering budget accessories and clothing at negotiable prices. Each tier serves a different shopper and a different budget. 1MG Lido Mall Sitting directly on MG Road at Trinity Circle, 1MG Lido Mall is the most accessible mall in the CBD. The brand mix leans mid-range to premium: H&M for basics, Fab India for Indian ethnic wear, Marks and Spencer for workwear, MAC and Estee Lauder for cosmetics, Puma and Nike for sportswear, and Aldo for footwear. The Bombay Store inside the mall carries curated Indian home decor, textiles, and gift items. Foodhall on the upper floor operates as a gourmet grocery store with imported cheeses, artisan breads, and specialty ingredients. A cinema screen, play zones, and restaurants round out the offering. Best for: Mid-range branded shopping, cosmetics, casual dining, catching a movie after shopping UB City Mall Located on Vittal Mallya Road, about a 10 minute walk south from MG Road, UB City is widely recognised as India’s first luxury mall. The brand roster includes Louis Vuitton, Burberry, Emporio Armani, Diesel, Paul Smith, and L’Occitane. The open air food court at UB City hosts some of Bangalore’s more talked about restaurants: Farzi Cafe for Indian fusion, Shiros for Japanese, Caperberry for modern European, and Cafe Mangii for wood fired pizzas. Sublime Galleria, an art gallery on the upper level, regularly rotates exhibitions. Skyye Lounge on the rooftop offers panoramic views of the city skyline. Best for: Luxury brand shopping, fine dining, art browsing, rooftop drinks Garuda Mall and Brigade Road Garuda Mall sits at the Brigade Road and Residency Road junction, roughly 500 metres from MG Road. The mall carries Zara, Calvin Klein, and a range of Indian and international brands alongside a multiplex, food court, gaming zone, and spa. Brigade Road itself is one of Bangalore’s most established retail streets. International sportswear brands like Asics, Adidas, Reebok, Skechers, and Under Armour operate standalone stores along this stretch. Indian menswear brands like Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Arrow, and Rare Rabbit sit alongside them. For visitors interested in budget shopping, Brigade Road also has several outlets selling export surplus clothing at lower price points. Best for: Mix of international and Indian brands, sportswear, multiplex entertainment, street browsing Cauvery Emporium and Karnataka Handicrafts Cauvery Handicrafts Emporium is the government run store for Karnataka state handicrafts, located directly on MG Road within a 5 minute walk from MG Road Metro Station (Exit A). The emporium stocks Mysore silk sarees, sandalwood carvings, rosewood artefacts, Channapatna wooden toys, Bidriware (silver inlaid metalwork from Bidar), and Karnataka coffee. Prices are fixed, and the quality is government certified, which removes the bargaining uncertainty that comes with buying these items from private vendors. Operating hours run from 10:00 AM to 7:30 PM. For silk saree shopping beyond Cauvery, Deepam Silks and Prasiddhi on MG Road carry dedicated Kanjivaram, Mysore silk, and Banarasi collections. If you are looking for a broader street shopping experience, Commercial Street is about 1.5 km from MG Road Metro Station and offers one of the most extensive budget shopping stretches in South India. Best for: Authentic Karnataka handicrafts, silk sarees, fixed price shopping, gifts and souvenirs Street Shopping and Budget Finds MG Road and Brigade Road both have sections of street vendors selling oxidised jewellery, hair accessories, phone cases, sunglasses, printed scarves, and budget clothing. Prices start as low as Rs 50 for accessories and Rs 200 for clothing items. Quality is mixed, so inspect stitching and material before paying. Bargaining is expected at street stalls. The area around Brigade Road near Garuda Mall has the densest cluster of street vendors, particularly active after 5:00 PM on weekdays and throughout the day on weekends. Note: Prices are approximate and may change based on season, demand, and availability. Where to Eat Around MG Road Bangalore The food scene across the MG Road district covers everything from Rs 70 filter coffee and dosas to Rs 3,000 per head fine dining. The restaurants cluster differently by street: MG Road itself has iconic standalone eateries, Church Street is the cafe and casual dining strip, and Brigade Road and Lavelle Road lean toward pubs that double as restaurants. Restaurants That Have Been Here for Decades Koshy’s Parade Cafe has operated on MG Road since 1940 and remains one of Bangalore’s most recognised names. The menu runs Anglo-Indian: mutton cutlets, egg burji, grilled fish, and filter coffee. A meal for two costs approximately Rs 600 to Rs 900. The crowd mixes retired regulars, college students, journalists, and tourists, and the wood panelled interior has not changed much in decades. Indian Coffee House on Church Street is another institution. The single page menu offers dosas, cutlets, omelettes, and coffee, all under Rs 100 per person. Waiters in white uniforms and turbans serve food at communal wooden tables. The experience belongs to a different Bangalore entirely, and it sits in the middle of the city’s most modern cafe strip. Ebony on Barton Centre, MG Road, serves North Indian and international cuisine across two floors with a terrace offering city views. The butter chicken here draws specific mention from repeat visitors. The Church Street Cafe Strip Church Street runs roughly 750 metres parallel to MG Road and has become Bangalore’s primary cafe and casual dining zone. The concentration is high enough that you can walk the full length in 15 minutes and pass over a dozen distinct eating options. Truffles is one of the most popular names on Church Street, known for American-style burgers, thick shakes, and generous portions. Expect a wait during weekend lunch hours. A meal for two costs around Rs 700 to Rs 1,000. Cafe Azzure sits on the fourth floor of a building on Church Street with a rooftop terrace overlooking the metro line. Continental and Italian dishes dominate the menu. Costs sit around Rs 800 for two. The Permit Room serves South Indian food with a cocktail bar twist: filter coffee cocktails, rasam shots, and modern plating of classic Karnataka dishes. A meal with drinks for two costs approximately Rs 1,500 to Rs 2,000. Mainland China on Church Street handles Chinese fine dining. Paragon covers Kerala-style biryani and seafood. Matteo Coffea works for coffee, desserts, and a quiet sit-down. The sheer variety within a 10 minute walking radius is what makes the mg road bangalore shopping guide incomplete without a food section. Budget Eats Under Rs 500 for Two Anand Sweets near Brigade Road serves chaat, sev puri, and South Indian snacks under Rs 200 for two. Street food carts around MG Road Metro Station sell vada pav, pani puri, and fresh juice for Rs 30 to Rs 80. If you are shopping on Brigade Road and need a quick fill before the evening, several budget Karnataka restaurants along the side lanes serve rice meals and thali plates for Rs 150 to Rs 250 per person. Nightlife Around MG Road: Pubs, Bars and Breweries Bangalore’s pub culture started on MG Road and Brigade Road in the 1980s, and the area still holds the highest concentration of bars, pubs, lounges, and breweries in the city. The district is compact enough that bar-hopping on foot between 3 or 4 spots in a single evening is practical. The Original Pubs Pecos on Brigade Road opened in the 1980s and is widely considered one of the first pubs in Bangalore. The interiors lean retro: dim lighting, classic rock on the speakers, beer pitchers, and simple bar food. A round for two costs around Rs 500 to Rs 800. Pecos does not try to be trendy, and that is precisely the point. Chin Lung on MG Road is another OG name. The menu is short, but the garlic chicken is a local favourite. The crowd is mixed, the prices are moderate, and the bar serves straightforward drinks without craft cocktail pretensions. For anyone writing or reading an mg road bangalore shopping guide, knowing these two names is baseline. The Pub in the basement of The Paul hotel on Brigade Road has pool tables, dart boards, and a pub food menu. It has operated for decades and draws a consistent after-work crowd. Craft Breweries and Lounges Arbor Brewing Company on Magrath Road (connecting to MG Road) is one of India’s earliest craft breweries. The Bangalore Bliss IPA and the Beachshack IPA are their best known brews. A pint costs between Rs 350 and Rs 500. The space also serves solid American-style food. Biere Club operates as a beer garden near Lavelle Road and brews its own range on site. The outdoor seating makes it a strong pick for groups. Hard Rock Cafe on St. Mark’s Road hosts weekly live bands and DJ nights. The combination of branded merchandise, live music, and a global menu makes it a reliable option for visitors who want a familiar format with local energy. Rooftop and Premium Spots Skyye Lounge at UB City sits on the top floor with 360 degree views of Bangalore. Drinks are premium priced (Rs 600 to Rs 1,200 per cocktail), and the crowd skews towards a dressed up, late evening demographic. Clear winter evenings offer the best visibility. The Tao Terraces at 1MG Lido Mall serves Pan-Asian cuisine with a terrace bar setup. Weekend nights tend to transition into a light party atmosphere after dinner service. Most pubs and bars in this district operate until 11:30 PM to 12:30 AM, depending on the establishment’s licence. Some lounges with late night licences stay open until 1:00 AM. Cover charges apply at a few spots during weekend nights, typically Rs 500 to Rs 1,500 per person, often redeemable against food and drinks. How to Reach MG Road Bangalore MG Road is one of the most connected locations in Bangalore across metro, bus, and cab networks. By Metro MG Road Metro Station on the Purple Line is the most direct route. The station sits between Trinity and Cubbon Park stations. Exit A leads to MG Road Boulevard and Cauvery Emporium. Exit B leads to Trinity Circle and the Brigade Road junction. Both exits connect easily to Church Street. Metro trains run daily from 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM, with Sunday service starting at 8:00 AM. The Purple Line connects MG Road to Whitefield, Indiranagar, Majestic, and locations across the east-west corridor. Trinity Metro Station, one stop east from MG Road Station, provides an alternative entry point closer to 1MG Lido Mall and the eastern end of the road. By Bus BMTC buses stop directly on MG Road. Multiple city bus routes from Majestic, Shivajinagar, Koramangala, and other parts of Bangalore terminate at or pass through MG Road. For travellers arriving from other cities, Majestic Bus Stand (Kempegowda Bus Station) is approximately 4 km from MG Road, reachable by metro in about 10 minutes on the Purple Line. From Bangalore Airport and Railway Station Kempegowda International Airport is roughly 35 to 40 km from MG Road. Cab or app-based rides take 60 to 90 minutes depending on traffic. Vayu Vajra airport buses operated by BMTC also connect the airport to the city centre. Bangalore City Railway Station (also called Krantivira Sangolli Rayanna or KSR Station) is about 4 km from MG Road. The station connects to Majestic Metro Station, from where MG Road is 3 stops east on the Purple Line. Travellers arriving in Bangalore by bus from Chennai, Hyderabad, Coorg, or other South Indian cities can check the Bangalore bus booking page for schedules and boarding points. Most zingbus routes in Bangalore use Majestic, Madiwala, Silk Board, and Electronic City as boarding and drop-off points, all of which connect to MG Road via metro or a short cab ride. You Might Also Like Commercial Street Bangalore: Timings, Shopping Guide — If MG Road covers branded retail and nightlife, Commercial Street covers budget ethnic wear, handcrafted jewellery, and fabric shopping across one of Bangalore’s oldest market streets. Bangalore to Coorg Bus: Complete Travel Guide — A weekend trip to Coorg’s coffee plantations and waterfalls pairs well with a Bangalore city day for travellers combining urban and nature experiences. Monsoon Getaways Near Bangalore by Bus — Chikmagalur, Wayanad, Jog Falls, and Kabini are all reachable by overnight bus for travellers looking to extend a Bangalore trip into the Western Ghats. Waterfalls Near Bangalore — Shivanasamudra, Chunchi Falls, and Hogenakkal make strong day trip additions after a day of MG Road shopping and dining. What to Know Before Spending a Day on MG Road A few patterns catch out first-time visitors and even some regulars. Knowing them ahead saves time, money, and a couple of avoidable frustrations. Park and Explore MG Road, Brigade Road, Church Street, and the connecting lanes are all within a 1 to 1.5 km radius. Taking a cab between spots inside this zone usually costs more in waiting time (traffic) than in fare. The most efficient approach is to arrive by metro at MG Road or Trinity station and cover the rest on foot. Avoid Weekend Crowds If you prefer a calmer shopping experience, go before 5:00 PM on a weekday. The street vendors set up their best displays in the evening, though, so the trade-off is real. Walk to UB City Visitors sometimes treat UB City as a different destination because the address says Vittal Mallya Road. It connects to MG Road through a short, well-lit walk. Combine it with dinner or rooftop drinks at Skyye after shopping on MG Road. Carry a Light Layer Bangalore’s weather stays pleasant most of the year, hovering between 18 and 30 degrees Celsius. But stepping from a warm afternoon into a heavily air-conditioned mall can feel sharp, especially during monsoon months when humidity is already high. Pay with UPI Malls, restaurants, cafes, and most pubs accept Google Pay, PhonePe, and card payments. Street vendors sometimes prefer cash, so keep Rs 500 to Rs 1,000 in small notes if you plan to buy from the Brigade Road pavement stalls. Book Pub Tables Early Popular spots like Hard Rock Cafe, Arbor, and The Permit Room fill up by 8:00 PM on Fridays and Saturdays. A reservation (most accept calls or online bookings) removes the 30 to 45 minute wait that walk-in groups face. One Road, Three Evenings Worth of Plans The MG Road Bangalore shopping guide covers more ground than most visitors expect from a single road because MG Road functions less as a single street and more as a district. The malls give you branded retail without the suburban drive. Cauvery Emporium gives you Karnataka at fixed prices. Church Street gives you 12 cafes in 750 metres. Brigade Road gives you shoes, beer, and karaoke in the same building. And all of it sits between two metro stations. For travellers heading to Bangalore from other cities, check current routes and schedules on the zingbus app to plan your arrival around a full day on this stretch. Frequently Asked Questions What Is MG Road Bangalore Famous For? MG Road Bangalore is famous for its concentration of shopping malls, branded retail stores, restaurants, cafes, pubs, and nightlife venues within a compact walkable stretch in the city’s Central Business District. Landmarks like 1MG Lido Mall, UB City, Cauvery Emporium, and Church Street all sit within or directly adjacent to this road. What Are the Best Malls on MG Road for Shopping? The best malls on MG Road for shopping are 1MG Lido Mall for mid-range to premium brands, UB City on Vittal Mallya Road for luxury labels, and Garuda Mall near Brigade Road for a mix of national and international brands. Each mall serves a different budget and shopping style. Is There Street Shopping on MG Road? Yes, there is street shopping on MG Road and especially on Brigade Road. Street vendors sell budget jewellery, accessories, scarves, sunglasses, and clothing. Prices start from Rs 50 and bargaining is expected. The stalls become most active after 5:00 PM. What Is Cauvery Emporium and Where Is It Located? Cauvery Emporium is a government run handicrafts store on MG Road, about 5 minutes on foot from MG Road Metro Station (Exit A). It sells Mysore silk sarees, sandalwood products, rosewood carvings, Channapatna toys, Bidriware, and Karnataka coffee at fixed prices. It operates from 10:00 AM to 7:30 PM. How Do You Reach MG Road Bangalore by Metro? You can reach MG Road Bangalore by taking the Purple Line of Namma Metro to MG Road Metro Station or Trinity Metro Station. Trains run daily from 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM, starting at 8:00 AM on Sundays. Exit A connects to MG Road Boulevard, and Exit B leads to Brigade Road junction. What Are the Best Pubs Near MG Road? The best pubs near MG Road include Pecos and The Pub on Brigade Road for classic pub vibes, Arbor Brewing Company on Magrath Road for craft beer, Hard Rock Cafe on St. Mark’s Road for live music, and Skyye Lounge at UB City for premium rooftop drinks. Most pubs operate from 11:30 PM to 12:30 AM. What Time Do Shops on MG Road Open and Close? Shops on MG Road and in the surrounding malls generally open between 10:00 AM and 11:00 AM. Malls close by 9:00 PM to 10:00 PM. Street vendors are active from late afternoon until about 9:00 PM. Restaurants and pubs stay open later, with most bars serving until 11:30 PM to 12:30 AM. Is MG Road Safe to Visit at Night? MG Road is generally safe to visit at night. The area remains active with pub and restaurant foot traffic until midnight, and the metro operates until 11:00 PM. Brigade Road and Church Street are well-lit and patrolled. Standard city precautions apply: stay on main roads, keep belongings secure, and use app-based cabs for late night returns. What Is the Best Food on Church Street Bangalore? Church Street Bangalore offers a wide variety of food, from Truffles for American-style burgers and shakes to Indian Coffee House for retro-style dosas and filter coffee under Rs 100. The Permit Room serves South Indian food with cocktail bar pairing, and Cafe Azzure offers rooftop continental dining. The street covers nearly every cuisine within a 750 metre walk. Can You Visit MG Road and Commercial Street on the Same Day? Yes, you can visit MG Road and Commercial Street on the same day since Commercial Street is approximately 1.5 km from MG Road Metro Station. A short auto or cab ride connects the two. Mornings at Commercial Street for ethnic wear and accessories, followed by evenings at MG Road for food and nightlife, is a practical combination. How Far Is MG Road from Bangalore Airport? MG Road is approximately 35 to 40 km from Kempegowda International Airport. A cab ride takes 60 to 90 minutes depending on traffic. BMTC Vayu Vajra airport buses also connect the airport to the city centre with stops near MG Road. What Should You Buy on MG Road Bangalore? Things worth buying on MG Road Bangalore include Mysore silk sarees and Karnataka handicrafts from Cauvery Emporium, international fashion brands from 1MG Lido Mall and Garuda Mall, luxury items from UB City, and budget jewellery and accessories from Brigade Road street vendors. The mg road bangalore shopping guide covers options from Rs 50 street finds to premium luxury purchases. Is There Parking Available Near MG Road? MG Road Metro Station does not have dedicated parking. The nearest paid parking is at Brigade Road, about 300 metres from the station. 1MG Lido Mall and Garuda Mall offer paid basement parking for visitors. Most visitors arrive by metro, auto, or cab given the central location and congested traffic. What Is the Best Time to Visit MG Road Bangalore? The best time to visit MG Road Bangalore is between October and February, when temperatures are most pleasant for walking between outdoor attractions. For daily timing, late afternoon (4:00 PM to 5:00 PM) lets you catch the tail end of shopping, move into dinner, and transition to nightlife without switching locations. Does MG Road Have a Weekly Off Day? MG Road does not have a universal weekly off day. Malls, showrooms, restaurants, and pubs operate seven days a week. Individual stores may occasionally close on specific days, but the area as a whole remains active throughout the week, with weekends being the busiest period.

title: Security Enablement for Sales: Stop the GRC Bottleneck
summary: Security enablement for sales teams means reps answer security questions in real time without pinging GRC. Here's how to set it up and why it works.
body_text: ‍ Security enablement for sales teams is the practice of giving sales reps accurate, real-time answers to security questions without forcing them to interrupt the GRC team. When done right, the rep stays unblocked, the GRC team stays focused, and the deal keeps moving. When done wrong, every prospect call that touches security stalls. ‍ It's 2:14pm on a Tuesday. Your sales rep is on a live call with a prospect who handles sensitive financial data. The prospect asks: "Are you SOC 2 Type II compliant? Where is our data stored? What encryption do you use at rest?" ‍ The rep knows the answer to the first question. Maybe. The second and third? No chance. So the rep does one of three things. They give a vague answer that erodes confidence. They say, "I'll get back to you on that," and kill the momentum. Or they Slack the GRC team mid-task, hoping someone is available. ‍ None of these is a good outcome. And the volume of these moments is greater than most teams realize: of the 100,000+ security questions Skypher has processed, 71.2% arrive as Excel files, 19.2% come through online portals like OneTrust and Archer, and 9.6% as Word documents. That's the formal questionnaire volume. The informal "quick security question on a call" volume is on top of that, and it lands directly on the sales team first. Why GRC teams become the sales security bottleneck Here's the dynamic that plays out at most SaaS and tech companies. The GRC team is small. Two people, sometimes three. They're responsible for maintaining compliance posture, managing audits, responding to security questionnaires, updating policies, and handling vendor risk assessments. They are not sitting around waiting for sales reps to ping them. ‍ But that's exactly what the sales team needs them to be. The sales team operates on a different clock, set by the prospect's calendar. When a prospect asks a security question on a live call, the window to give a confident answer is measured in seconds. ‍ The GRC team's clock is set by audit deadlines, questionnaire queues, and project timelines. These two clocks rarely sync up. Without security enablement for sales in place, the GRC team becomes a synchronous dependency for an asynchronous job. The hidden cost of delayed security answers in sales When a sales rep can't answer a security question in real time, the damage is subtle but real. Three costs compound at once. ‍ First, the prospect loses confidence. Security buyers are evaluating whether your company takes this seriously. A hesitant answer or a "let me check" signals that your team doesn't have its act together. Even if you follow up with the right answer two hours later, the impression is already set. ‍ Second, the deal slows down. Every "I'll get back to you" adds a round trip. The rep sends a Slack message. The GRC person sees it between tasks, types a response, the rep relays it over email. What could have been settled in 30 seconds on a call now takes a day. Multiply that across a pipeline and you're looking at real revenue impact. ‍ Third, the GRC team gets fragmented. Every interruption pulls someone out of deep work. Answering a security questionnaire requires focus. When a GRC analyst is halfway through a 200-question assessment and gets pinged for a quick answer, they lose context. The "quick" answer takes 2 minutes, but the context switch costs 20. This is the deeper reason your security questionnaire knowledge base keeps failing — it isn't built to serve sales conversations, only audit ones. Why sales is the GRC team's most important internal customer This framing matters. If you run a GRC function at a SaaS company, your sales team is one of your primary internal customers. They depend on your knowledge to close deals. When the GRC team is a bottleneck, deals stall. ‍ But the solution isn't "be more available." You can't scale human availability with a two-person team. And hiring another GRC analyst just to answer ad hoc questions from sales is not a realistic budget conversation. ‍ The solution is to decouple the sales team's need for answers from the GRC team's availability. That decoupling is what security enablement for sales actually delivers. What real security enablement for sales looks like There are a few practical approaches, and the best teams combine more than one. ‍ A searchable security knowledge base. Your GRC team already knows the answers to 90% of the questions sales reps get asked: SOC 2 status, data residency, encryption standards, subprocessor lists, incident response timelines. These answers don't change week to week. Put them in a searchable format that sales reps can access during calls. A purpose-built smart security knowledge base eliminates a huge percentage of interruptions on its own. ‍ A Slack integration for self-service security answers. Sales reps live in Slack. If they can type a question in a channel and get an accurate, sourced answer back in seconds, they never need to interrupt anyone. The GRC team maintains the source content. The tool serves the answers. The rep stays unblocked. ‍ An AI agent trained on your security posture. This is where the real shift happens. Instead of maintaining a static FAQ, you feed your completed questionnaires, policies, and security documentation into a system that can answer new questions accurately. The sales rep asks "Do we support SAML SSO?" and gets a precise answer with the source document referenced. No human in the loop. This is also how teams deflect 30% of security questionnaires through an automated trust center — the same source of truth serves both prospects and reps. ‍ The key word in all of these is "accurate." A self-service tool that gives wrong answers is worse than no tool at all. The GRC team needs to trust that what the sales team is getting is correct. That means the system needs to pull from verified, up-to-date sources, not generate answers from thin air. Why GRC teams gain the most from sales security enablement Here's what's counterintuitive: the biggest beneficiary of self-service security answers isn't the sales team. It's the GRC team. ‍ When sales reps stop interrupting with one-off questions, the GRC team gets uninterrupted blocks of time. Those blocks are where real work happens. Completing questionnaires. Preparing for audits. Updating policies. Building the compliance infrastructure that actually protects the company. ‍ This is why teams like Adobe, Deel, and McKinsey use Skypher to centralize their security knowledge. Adobe went from spending two weeks on a single security questionnaire to completing them in about two hours. With 200+ enterprise customers and 96% answer accuracy across every major format, Skypher's security questionnaire automation platform gives the GRC team one source of truth that sales, presales, and customer-facing teams can all draw from. The time savings doesn't just come from automating the questionnaire itself. It comes from the GRC team being able to focus without constant context switches from sales. How to roll out security enablement for sales in practice If you're a GRC lead reading this, here's a practical path forward. ‍ Start by auditing the questions your sales team actually asks. Pull the last month of Slack messages, emails, and meeting notes where a sales rep asked you a security question. You'll find that 80% of them are the same 20 questions. ‍ Document those answers in a format your sales team can search. Even a shared Google Doc is better than nothing. A dedicated tool is better than a Google Doc. For a longer playbook on structuring this process, see Skypher's best practices for automating your security questionnaire response process . Then evaluate whether an AI-powered solution can handle the long tail. The 20% of questions that aren't in your FAQ are the ones that still require judgment. But a well-trained system with access to your completed questionnaires and policies can handle most of those too. ‍ The goal is simple: your sales team should be able to get accurate security answers without requiring a human from the GRC team to be available at that exact moment. The GRC team stays focused. The sales team stays unblocked. Deals move forward. ‍ That's not a nice-to-have. For a growing SaaS company with enterprise buyers, security enablement for sales is operational infrastructure. FAQ ‍ What is security enablement for sales? Security enablement for sales is the set of tools, content, and workflows that let sales reps answer security questions in real time without pulling in the GRC team for every request. It typically combines a searchable security knowledge base, a Slack or browser integration, and an AI layer trained on your completed questionnaires and policies. Why does the GRC team become a sales bottleneck? The GRC team is usually two or three people responsible for audits, questionnaire queues, and policy work — none of which is interruptible. When sales reps need answers during live calls, the synchronous request collides with deep-focus GRC work. Without self-service security answers, every "quick question" costs the GRC analyst around 20 minutes of lost context for a 2-minute answer. How do you answer security questions on sales calls without slowing the deal? The fastest path is a self-service security knowledge base the rep can search during the call, backed by an AI agent that pulls from completed questionnaires and policies. Reps get an accurate, sourced answer in seconds, the prospect keeps confidence, and the GRC team is never interrupted. Can AI handle presales security questions accurately? Yes, when the AI is grounded in your verified security documentation rather than generating answers from scratch. Skypher reaches 96% answer accuracy by pulling from a maintained knowledge base of completed questionnaires, policies, and trust center content — which is also why teams like Adobe cut questionnaire turnaround from two weeks to two hours. Should sales reps have direct access to security documentation? They should have access to a curated layer designed for them, not the raw policy library. The GRC team maintains a single source of truth; the sales-facing tool surfaces only the answers that are approved, current, and phrased for a prospect-facing context. That separation keeps reps fast without compromising what the GRC team certifies as accurate. ‍

title: Face the Facts: 3 Myths About Injectable Neurotoxin Treatments
summary: Navigating the world of cosmetic treatments sometimes feels like taking a midnight hike on a foggy mountain. Sure, somewhere there's solid...
body_text: Navigating the world of cosmetic treatments can sometimes feels like taking a midnight hike on a foggy mountain. Sure, somewhere there's solid ground — but one wrong step and things could go sideways (or downhill) in a second. Let’s clear up some of that fog! Today, we’re tackling three of the most pervasive myths about injectable treatments for frown lines and wrinkles and sharing some interesting facts along the way. Myth #1: All Neurotoxin Injections Are the Same All neurotoxin injection treatments might seem the same on the surface, because they offer the same basic function — releasing the muscles responsible for wrinkles. But there are actually many differences between the available neurotoxin injection treatments for wrinkles, from a tox’s molecular formulation to its purification process. Toxins differ by formulation The formulation of a neurotoxin can have a huge impact on its results. While all ‘tox treatments are made from botulinum toxin type A, other ingredients in the formulation can and do differ. Most injectable wrinkle treatments include other ingredients, such as buffers and stabilizers. This is why it’s super important to disclose any allergies to your injection specialist — just in case you happen to be allergic to one of the protein complexes in the tox injection you’re planning! Manufacturing and purification processes vary, too You know how every baking show contestant has to make the same recipe, but all of their cakes somehow turn out looking totally different? Think of the neurotoxin manufacturing process the same way. While all injectable neurotoxins are made from the same main ingredient (botulinum toxin type A, in case you already forgot), the way each product is purified and processed can lead to different results and onset times. For example, Jeuveau's proprietary Hi-Pure™ Technology includes additional manufacturing steps, to create an ultra-pure (at least 95%) tox that’s designed to remain within its field of injection without spreading. Injections can be fast-acting, long-lasting or both. Timing is everything, and it’s another way neurotoxin injection treatments can differ. Some treatments work faster than others, and some last longer than others. Comparing tox options? You’ll want to know: How quickly they start creating visible effects (known as the “onset time”) How long those effects last (known as the “duration of results”) Some neurotoxins can produce results within a few days, while others may take a week or more to begin showing on your face. The results of some injections will wear off within a few months, while the effects of others can last up to six months. That’s why when considering your areas of concern, budget and desired results, your injector will ask, “What’s most important to you?” Myth #2: Neurotoxin Treatments Are Only For Vain People First of all, we’d like to be the first to say that there’s nothing wrong with aging OR obsessing about vanity. It’s wonderful to love your own look, especially as you grow older . And it’s also totally fine to shape the way you want to look — whether by creating your own personal clothing style, experimenting with makeup or choosing cosmetic treatments and procedures. People schedule injectable treatments for a myriad of reasons. You might choose to proactively begin getting different treatments as a preventive measure. You might book a treatment before a big event like a wedding or school reunion. You might get injections once and never again, or you might look forward to your quarterly standing appointment with your injector. Our take on it? If injections make you feel more like the best and brightest version of yourself (for us, that’s the version who looks like they got 9 hours of sleep last night), then they’re a great part of your overall beauty routine. No matter your reason for choosing a cosmetic procedure, it’s your decision. So reject the stigma and feel empowered about your choice! Myth #3: Injectable Treatments Are Unsafe Or Unnatural Of course no one wants to put something dangerous in their body. But labeling all injectable treatments as unsafe or unnatural is like saying “All snack foods are unhealthy!” Tell that to my bag of baby carrots. Every injectable treatment, including Jeuveau , is backed by rigorous testing and must be FDA-approved before it becomes available for consumer use. They don't just hand those approvals out like free samples at a supermarket, y’all. There are years of clinical studies and documentation behind every injectable cosmetic treatment. The active ingredient in neurotoxins - botulinum toxin - is a substance found in nature that has been refined into a purified protein and finished aesthetic product. When correctly administered, it is well-tolerated by most people. Common side effects can include bruising or swelling at the injection site, headache and eyelid or brow drooping. Of course, there can also be serious risks with neurotoxins. Rarely, injections can spread from their targeted site and cause more serious side effects. So much for those myths. Let's do a quick recap, shall we? Not all neurotoxin injections are created equal. And they definitely don’t need to look unnatural. While all neurotoxin treatments share the same goal — to help release facial wrinkles and give you a more relaxed, refreshed look — their differences are key. Having the right information when you’re comparing injectable wrinkle treatments is incredibly important. Thanks for taking the time to read through these myths and learn the truth!

title: The CFO's guide to tail spend management strategies
summary: Learn tail spend management strategies for multi-entity CFOs, covering tail spend analysis, frameworks, and software to govern spend across entities.
body_text: What is tail spend and why is it bigger than a procurement problem Tail spend covers the long list of small, fragmented purchases sitting outside your negotiated contracts and preferred vendors. Think one-off software subscriptions, small consultants, and minor equipment orders, the kind of spend too small to justify a formal sourcing process. Most procurement teams treat this as a cleanup task. For a CFO running multiple entities, it's something bigger: Long tail spend management isn't about tidying up a vendor list; it's about visibility across every entity making small purchases on their own. A single entity might tolerate a messy tail. Across three or four entities, in different currencies, that same tail becomes real exposure. Tail spend has the least standardised approval process of any spend category, which is exactly why it drifts out of policy first. Tail spend isn't the same as maverick spend, and long tail spend management has to account for both. Tail spend is defined by size: small and scattered. Maverick spend is defined by noncompliance, purchases made outside approved vendors, regardless of size. The real question isn't how much you're spending on the tail. It's how much control you actually have over it. Examples of tail spend categories Tail spend shows up in a few recurring forms across most organisations, regardless of industry. Software subscriptions and one-off SaaS tools purchased outside a central contract Small consultants or contractors engaged for a single project Minor equipment or office supply purchases Ad hoc marketing spend: event costs, freelance design, small campaign tools One-time vendor payments with no recurring relationship Duplicate subscriptions across entities for the same function Benefits of strategic tail spend management A tail spend management strategy pays off well beyond cost savings. CFOs who treat this as governance, not cleanup, gain something harder to quantify but more valuable long term: a finance operation that scales without needing more people to watch it. [Table:1] Tail spend management challenges Most tail spend management strategies fail for the same reason: the spend was never visible in the first place. It sits scattered across entities, disconnected systems, and vendors nobody formally tracks, which is exactly why a proper tail spend management framework has to start with the problem, not the fix. [Table:2] Tail spend management strategies Most tail spend management strategies fall apart at scale because they were designed for a single finance team reviewing a single vendor list. What works for one entity rarely survives contact with five, unless the strategy was built to travel. Consolidating suppliers and sourcing rationalisation Check vendor overlap across entities rather than within a single one. A CFO overseeing multiple subsidiaries will often find three regional teams paying three different vendors for the same software category, each negotiated on its own. Categories with the highest vendor count hide the most inefficiency, sometimes more than categories with higher total spend. Centralise sourcing visibility first Full centralisation tends to create bottlenecks. A lighter approach works better: get a shared view of who's buying what and where vendors overlap, then let purchasing stay decentralised. That partial visibility alone captures most of the available savings. Sort vendors into retain, eliminate, or treat as one-off Some vendors are worth keeping and renegotiating. Others have outlived their usefulness and should be cut. Everything else, a single-use purchase that won't recur, just needs a quick, simple payment process rather than a full vendor setup. Enforce policy at the point of purchase Most software available today reports on spend after it happens. A better system checks a purchase against policy the moment someone tries to make it, in real time, applying the same rule whether the transaction originates in Singapore, Vietnam, or anywhere else the business operates. Aspire's expense management and approval flows are built around exactly this, so oversight scales as entities are added, without adding headcount to watch each one. Review the tail regularly for vendors that no longer belong there Some vendors grow past the point where they should sit in the tail at all, rising spend, rising risk, or both. A quarterly review catches these and moves them into strategic sourcing with a proper contract, keeping the tail from quietly absorbing spend that needs real oversight. The future of tail spend management Tail spend management trends over the next few years point toward one direction: less manual review, more systems making the low-risk calls on their own. The categories and frameworks stay the same, but the amount of human time spent applying them keeps shrinking. For a CFO planning finance operations two or three years out, this matters more than any single feature comparison today. Agentic systems are starting to handle routine approvals end to end, not just flag them for a human to click through. The finance team's role shifts from approving transactions to setting the policy those systems follow. Real-time policy checks are replacing periodic audits. Instead of finding a problem vendor in a quarterly review, the system stops the transaction before it clears. Cross-entity data is becoming the default view, not a report someone builds manually. As more finance stacks consolidate onto a single platform, entity-level silos matter less. The definition of tail spend management software is shifting from a reporting tool to something closer to an operating layer, one that executes financial policy rather than just recording what happened after the fact. The metrics worth tracking as this shifts: percentage of tail spend running under automated policy, active vendor count per category, and how often a flagged transaction actually needed the review it got. Rising automation with a shrinking review rate is the sign the framework is working. Conclusion Tail spend rarely looks urgent until it's already expensive to fix. CFOs who stay ahead of it treat it as a governance decision, set once at the policy level and applied consistently across every entity, currency, and buyer. The right software then enforces that policy automatically, flagging only what needs attention. This is the shift underway across finance teams: from reviewing spend after it happens to governing it as it happens. This is the gap Aspire is built to close for multi-entity finance teams in Singapore and beyond. Expense management and approval flows apply policy at the point of transaction, budgets enforce category-level limits automatically, and a multi-currency account means cross-entity visibility doesn't require manual conversion or a monthly export. For a CFO scaling into new entities, that's what governing tail spend actually looks like in practice – a system that already knows the policy and applies it without being asked. FAQs What are the 4 pillars of strategic sourcing? Spend analysis, sourcing, contract management, and supplier management. Together they cover the full lifecycle of a sourcing decision, from spotting savings opportunities in your data to actually selecting suppliers, locking in compliant contracts, and maintaining the relationship long after signing. What are the 4 categories of spend? Direct spend, indirect spend, tail spend, and maverick spend. Direct and indirect split spend by what it's used for: production versus operations. Tail and maverick split it by how well it's managed: tail spend is low-value and often overlooked; maverick spend is any purchase made outside the approved process, regardless of size. What's the difference between tail spend and indirect spend? Tail spend sits inside indirect spend, but the two aren't the same thing. Indirect spend covers all operational costs that don't go into the final product, things like software, marketing, and facilities. Tail spend is the smaller, low-value slice of that: purchases too infrequent or too small to justify a formal contract. What percentage of spend is tail spend? Tail spend typically makes up around 80% of an organisation's transactions but only 20% of total spend value. Why is tail spend difficult to manage? It's scattered across disconnected systems, has no clear owner, and its transaction volume makes manual review impractical. How can software reduce tail spend? By enforcing policy automatically at the point of purchase, flagging only what falls outside policy instead of relying on manual review after the fact. What is tail spend sourcing? The process of consolidating and rationalising tail vendors, checking for overlap across categories and entities rather than sourcing each purchase individually.

title: Is your data center AI-ready? Ask these five questions.
summary: Your organization may be eager to implement AI initiatives, but is your data center ready? Our blog post explores the five questions to ask.
body_text: Eagerness to implement AI initiatives is a start. But then come the practicalities: is your data center truly ready to support the full potential of AI? Infrastructure limitations, data challenges, operational complexity, and security concerns could become barriers to scaling AI. Before investing in new AI models and applications, IT leaders should assess whether their data center and operating environment are ready Asking five questions can identify areas of your data center that need attention or improvement to support your AI ambitions. Do you have the necessary infrastructure? Your infrastructure lays the foundation for technology innovation, and it's as important as a house’s foundation. AI workloads require an environment made for agility, scalability, and seamless integration, and capable of handling AI’s intense data flows. Without the proper infrastructure, even the most advanced AI capabilities can sit idle, unable to deliver on their promise. AI’s power hinges on robust, scalable hardware, and your data center must support the unique compute, storage, and network demands AI workloads require. That means considering the performance and capabilities of all your systems and hardware, including your servers, storage, networking, and cooling. For best results, make sure your systems are integrated end-to-end. Manual processes often become bottlenecks for AI initiatives. Automation and intelligent operations can accelerate deployment of infrastructure resources, improve efficiency, and reduce operational complexity. Does your data center have sufficient power? Implementing AI initiatives requires attention to your organization’s GPU power density. Legacy racks built for 5 kilowatts can't support the 20-kilowatt demands of modern AI infrastructure. Without enough power, your AI ambitions risk stalling before they start. To gain a holistic view of your data center’s AI-readiness, consider: The amount of power your current setup can reliably supply The ability of cooling systems to efficiently manage the extra heat Whether these elements can work harmoniously to sustain continuous, intensive AI processes. Your data center requires a careful reassessment of power capacity and cooling infrastructure to support the heavy lifting AI workloads bring. Is your cybersecurity comprehensive? AI often handles sensitive customer information and proprietary corporate data, and your data center cybersecurity must be strong enough to protect it. A multi-layered security approach featuring physical safeguards, robust network defenses, and strict access controls can keep your intellectual property secure and your AI innovations safe. Organizations also should consider regulatory compliance requirements for AI usage and risks like unauthorized access to data, model manipulation, and data leakage. Comprehensive security strategy protects infrastructure and the AI ecosystem it supports. How much do you value cost consistency? Maintaining consistent costs each year is a business strategy for some businesses, with predictable budgeting allowing them to plan confidently without surprises derailing progress. They appreciate the control and visibility into data center controls, especially given the possibility of shifting cloud pricing. In contrast, other organizations have the capacity to embrace variable investments and prefer to roll with shifts to seize new opportunities. Understanding your company’s tolerance and aligning your data center strategy accordingly gives you an advantage as you ready your data center for increased AI use. Applying FInOps principles can help balance innovation with cost control as AI adoption scales. Have you planned for future growth? The “perfect house” changes over the years because of job and commuting shifts, new additions to the family, children leaving for college, downsizing, and aging. In the same way, data center demands change over time. Especially because AI isn’t static. Workload demands grow, sometimes exponentially. You need the ability to easily scale your data center to handle new workloads and AI initiatives. From scaling processing power and storage to expanding network capacity and cooling systems, flexibility is key. Whether your AI footprint expands organically or through strategic moves like acquisitions, your data center will adapt swiftly and seamlessly if you design infrastructure with built-in agility. Ensure your data center is AI ready Increasing your data center’s reliability, resilience, and issue-resolution speed can optimize performance. title: Sunrun Launches Distributed AI Data Center Pilot Backed By Existing Home Energy Generation
summary: America's largest on-site home generation and backup energy provider takes first step toward converting 1.1 million existing customers into…...
body_text: Sunrun Launches Distributed AI Data Center Pilot Backed By Existing Home Energy Generation July 08, 2026 8:00 AM EDT Download as PDF America's largest on-site home generation and backup energy provider takes first step toward converting 1.1 million existing customers into a nationwide compute network for distributed AI workload processing — unlocking more customer value and a new compute revenue stream SAN FRANCISCO, July 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sunrun (Nasdaq: RUN), America's largest provider of home battery storage, solar, and home-to-grid power plants, today launched a distributed AI compute pilot program . The pilot marks Sunrun's first step into distributed edge computing, a new business category that the company believes represents a high-margin revenue opportunity leveraging its existing energy infrastructure, large customer base, and grid service capabilities. Following a successful proof of concept that demonstrated revenue generation and high demand for distributed compute, Sunrun is expanding the pilot to place numerous compute nodes in homes equipped with Sunrun solar and battery storage systems. Sunrun is coordinating the selling of inference capacity to enterprise compute buyers, while also testing the nodes under a variety of conditions and rate structures to gather operational data and information. Participating homeowners are compensated for hosting the compute nodes. "AI companies are scrambling to secure greater access to energy and computing power,” said Sunrun President and Chief Revenue Officer Paul Dickson. “Over nearly two decades, we have perfected our ability to operationalize, finance, and scale distributed assets. We are now using our leadership position in distributed home energy and proven infrastructure to bring compute closer to the sources of energy and inference.” AI inference demand is growing at approximately 35% annually and is projected by McKinsey to surpass training as the dominant AI workload by 2030, representing more than half of all AI compute. Unlike AI training — which requires massive, tightly synchronized clusters — inference is modular, geographically distributable, and highly sensitive to latency. That makes it a natural fit for edge deployment close to end users, and a natural fit for Sunrun. Sunrun's distributed footprint of more than 1.1 million existing customers represent an addressable deployment base and gives the company a structural advantage hyperscalers can’t quickly replicate. Where a traditional data center can take years to permit, build, and interconnect, Sunrun's distributed deployment model can add significant inference capacity in a fraction of the time. Advantages of Sunrun's Distributed Compute Model Just as Sunrun has helped democratize energy by enabling households to generate, store, and share their own power, this distributed data center model enables American households to play a direct role in powering the nation's AI future and share in the economic opportunity it creates. For hyperscalers, it provides a flexible, scalable source of compute capacity that complements centralized data centers and accelerates AI deployment. Geographic Flexibility: By placing compute nodes behind the meter, Sunrun mitigates regional threats of rising utility rates, overloaded grids, and power supply shortages. Scale With New and Existing Customers : Sunrun can reach meaningful compute scale across its growing customer base of over 1.1 million nationwide without the lead time of new data center development. Speed to Compute: Deployed in the built environment, Sunrun's distributed nodes eliminate land acquisition, transmission buildout, and utility interconnection queues. Existing Service Infrastructure: Sunrun already monitors and services energy equipment on more than a million homes — an operational foundation immediately available to support distributed compute at scale. Backup Power: Distributed compute nodes are paired with Sunrun's onsite battery systems, allowing data processing to continue operations through certain grid outages. Grid Resilience, Not Grid Strain: Rather than adding load pressure to already congested regions, Sunrun's distributed model improves utilization of existing electrical infrastructure, turning the network into a grid asset as well as a compute asset. Maximizing System Value: Sunrun's systems and controls optimize the compute nodes in concert with the customer’s energy consumption patterns, participation in grid services, and the customer’s electricity rate structure. Customer Compensation: Consistent with Sunrun's strategy to expand customer value, participants are compensated for hosting compute nodes, extending Sunrun's value proposition and strengthening customer retention. Sunrun’s distributed compute pilot is a distinct and separate initiative, but complements the company’s recently announced agreement with Renew Home and Tesla to aggregate more than 16 gigawatts of flexible home energy capacity for hyperscalers and utilities. Compute capacity deployed onsite at customer homes can serve the same surging AI demand that is driving hyperscalers to seek every available path to new energy capacity. Sunrun expects to complete the pilot over the coming months and will assess results against defined milestones, compute performance, and homeowner experience before determining the scale, speed and customer offering of a broader rollout. The company is actively in discussions with enterprise compute offtakers, homebuilders, and utility partners to structure the commercial and deployment frameworks that would support expansion. To learn more and join the waitlist, visit sunrun.com/compute . About Sunrun Sunrun Inc. (Nasdaq: RUN) is America’s largest provider of home battery storage, solar, and home-to-grid power plants. As the pioneer of home energy systems offered through a no-upfront-cost subscription model, Sunrun empowers customers nationwide with greater energy control, security, and independence. Sunrun supports the grid by providing on-demand dispatchable power that helps prevent blackouts and lowers energy costs. Learn more at www.sunrun.com . title: Ken-Betwa River Interlinking Project | Why Tribals are Protesting (UPSC)
summary: Why is the Ken-Betwa Project making headlines? Understand the tribal protests in M.P, project benefits, environmental concerns and the way ahead. Read now!
body_text: Why in the News? The Ken-Betwa River Interlinking Project is back in the news after tribal communities in Madhya Pradesh intensified their protests over displacement, rehabilitation, and environmental concerns. In July 2026, affected families staged Jal Satyagraha, Chita Andolan (Pyre Protest), and hunger strikes , demanding fair compensation, protection of forest rights, and greater transparency in the project's implementation. The protests gained national attention after police cleared the protest site, bringing the debate over development versus tribal rights back into focus. About the Ken-Betwa River Interlinking Project The Ken-Betwa River Interlinking Project (KBLP) is India's first river interlinking project under the National Perspective Plan . It aims to transfer surplus water from the Ken River to the Betwa River to address water scarcity in the Bundelkhand region of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. The project is expected to improve irrigation, provide drinking water, and generate hydropower while supporting the region's socio-economic development. Key Facts About the Project The project is being executed by the National Water Development Agency (NWDA) under the Ministry of Jal Shakti through the Ken-Betwa Link Project Authority (KBLPA) . The project covers Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh , with most of the project infrastructure located in Madhya Pradesh. It connects the Ken River , a tributary of the Yamuna, with the Betwa River , another major Yamuna tributary. The project is estimated to cost over ₹44,000 crore (with revisions based on implementation and inflation). Main Components of the Project Construction of the Daudhan Dam on the Ken River. A 221-km Ken-Betwa Link Canal to transfer water. Low-Level Tunnel, High-Level Tunnel, barrages, and powerhouses for water regulation and electricity generation. Project Phases Phase I: Construction of the Daudhan Dam, link canal, tunnels, and hydropower facilities. Phase II: Development of the Lower Orr Dam, Kotha Barrage, and Bina Complex to further expand irrigation coverage. Objectives of the Project The Ken-Betwa River Interlinking Project aims to improve water availability in the drought-prone Bundelkhand region while supporting agriculture, livelihoods, and regional development. Its key objectives include: Address Water Scarcity in Bundelkhand: The primary objective is to transfer surplus water from the Ken River to the water-deficient Betwa River to reduce recurring water shortages in parts of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. Expand Irrigation Facilities: The project seeks to increase irrigation coverage across drought-prone districts, enabling farmers to cultivate more land, improve crop yields, and reduce dependence on erratic monsoon rainfall. Provide Drinking Water: Another key goal is to ensure a reliable supply of safe drinking water to millions of people living in urban and rural areas of the Bundelkhand region. Generate Clean Energy: The project includes the development of hydropower and solar power infrastructure to support renewable energy generation and strengthen the region's power supply. Boost Agricultural and Economic Development: By improving water availability, the project aims to enhance agricultural productivity, increase farmers' incomes, create employment opportunities, and promote overall socio-economic development. Improve Water Resource Management: The project aims to optimise the use of available river water through inter-basin transfer, ensuring more balanced and efficient utilisation of water resources. Strengthen Climate and Drought Resilience: The project seeks to reduce the impact of recurring droughts in Bundelkhand by ensuring a more dependable water supply for agriculture, domestic use, and other essential needs. Also see: List of Major Dams of India for UPSC: Oldest, Longest & Highest Dams in India Expected Benefits of the Ken-Betwa Project The Ken-Betwa River Interlinking Project is expected to deliver significant economic, social, and environmental benefits to the drought-prone Bundelkhand region. Expanded Irrigation Coverage: The project will provide irrigation to approximately 10.6 lakh hectares of agricultural land, improving crop productivity and reducing dependence on monsoon rainfall. Improved Drinking Water Supply: It is expected to ensure a reliable supply of drinking water to nearly 62 lakh people across several districts of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. Clean Energy Generation: The project will generate around 103 MW of hydropower and 27 MW of solar power , contributing to renewable energy production and regional energy security. Drought Mitigation: By improving water availability, the project aims to reduce the impact of recurring droughts in the Bundelkhand region, strengthening water security for agriculture, households, and industries. Regional Economic Development: Better water infrastructure is expected to boost agricultural income, create employment opportunities, and support the overall socio-economic development of the region. Enhanced Water Resource Management: The inter-basin transfer of water will promote more efficient utilisation of available water resources and help address regional water imbalances. Also read: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) - UPSC Notes Why Are Tribals Protesting Against the Project? In July 2026, affected families staged Jal Satyagraha, hunger strikes, and Chita Andolan (Pyre Protest), demanding protection of their land, forest rights, fair rehabilitation, and greater transparency in the project's implementation. 1. Displacement of Tribal Communities The construction of the Daudhan Dam will submerge several villages, displacing thousands of families, including a large number of Scheduled Tribes. Many fear losing their ancestral homes and traditional way of life. 2. Loss of Forest-Based Livelihoods Tribal communities depend on forests for farming, fishing, grazing, and collecting minor forest produce. The submergence of forest land threatens both their livelihoods and the rights recognised under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 . 3. Rehabilitation and Compensation Concerns Protesters claim that compensation is inadequate and that rehabilitation plans do not fully address their long-term needs. They are demanding fair compensation, land-for-land rehabilitation, and proper resettlement before displacement. 4. Environmental Impact A major concern is the submergence of parts of the Panna Tiger Reserve , which could lead to forest loss, habitat fragmentation, and adverse impacts on biodiversity. 5. Violation of Tribal Rights Many tribal groups allege that Gram Sabhas were not meaningfully consulted and that the provisions of the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and the PESA Act, 1996, have not been adequately implemented. Also read: Important Tribes in India [UPSC Notes] Way Forward "Development that destroys the environment is not development; it is destruction." — Sunderlal Bahuguna The Ken-Betwa River Interlinking Project must strike a balance between development, environmental conservation, and tribal rights. A sustainable and inclusive approach is essential for its long-term success. Provide fair compensation, land-for-land rehabilitation, and timely resettlement before displacement. Strictly implement the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and PESA Act, 1996, ensuring meaningful participation of Gram Sabhas in decision-making. Minimise forest loss through scientific planning, afforestation, wildlife conservation, and continuous ecological monitoring. Build trust through regular public consultations, independent social and environmental audits, and transparent implementation. Complement river interlinking with watershed development, rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, and efficient irrigation practices. A truly successful river-linking project will be the one that delivers water security while safeguarding forests, wildlife, and the rights and dignity of indigenous communities. title: From Vision to Execution: Already Living the Agentic AI Future
summary: Cristian Coccia, VP SEMEA & Enterprise Sales EMEA, reflects on how local markets like Italy and Spain are driving this shift, proving that transparency, trust and infrastructure are what turn AI ambition into measurable campaign results.
body_text: Six months ago, if you had asked most people in our industry when agentic AI would start to reshape programmatic advertising, the honest answer would likely have been “soon, but not yet.” Today, that answer no longer fits. The future didn’t arrive on a fixed date. It came gradually, first as a concept we discussed, then as a reality taking shape inside campaigns, data pipelines, and commercial strategies. Milan, Madrid: Two Cities, One Trajectory Over the past half‑year, I’ve had the privilege of seeing that shift up close, not as an abstract trend, but as something tangible and measurable in our daily work with clients, publishers, and partners across our markets. In March, we gathered our business community in Milan for one of our most forward-looking PubAcademy sessions. The subject was bold: agentic AI, presented as a genuine turning point for digital advertising. The room was charged with curiosity and healthy skepticism. Together we explored questions that are central to our industry’s future: Who leads when AI drives decisions? How do we maintain trust as technology evolves faster than organisations? And can AI create true marketing value rather than just efficiency gains? The insight from Milan was pivotal. We were no longer debating whether agentic AI would transform programmatic trading, but how fast and who would be ready to act. Only three months later, at PubAcademy Madrid, that conversation took a dramatic step forward. The tone had shifted from ideas to impact. Real campaigns running across the open internet, using agentic AI throughout their whole lifecycle, and outperforming benchmarks. In a single quarter, we moved from vision to execution, a clear sign of how fast the market is evolving. The Question Has Changed For years, the operating question was when AI would become fully functional in programmatic advertising. That question no longer applies. Agentic AI is already planning, managing, and optimising media in real time, freeing teams to focus on creativity, strategy, and long term client outcomes. The new question is how quickly the rest of the market can keep pace. Scaling agentic AI is not about flipping a switch. It depends on solid foundations: solid infrastructure, verifiable decision logic, accountable data flows, and transparency. Buyers and publishers now want to understand not just results, but reasoning; what signals informed decisions and how those signals shaped performance. That depth of insight cannot be retrofitted. It has to be designed into the ecosystem from the start. This is exactly where PubMatic’s approach proves its value. Long before the industry spoke about agentic systems, we built our technology around openness, interoperability, and trust. That groundwork now enables agentic AI to operate responsibly and effectively across the supply chain. Markets That Drive the Shift One of the most inspiring aspects of this transformation has been the proactive role of local markets such as Italy and Spain, to name a couple. Our regional teams, agencies, publishers, and brands have not waited for global directives; they have experimented, tested, and refined what agentic AI can achieve under real campaign conditions. This local momentum matters. Global innovation only delivers sustainable value when it is grounded in local execution, driven by people who understand their markets, clients, and data realities. The conversations in Milan and Madrid were not isolated. They were two chapters of one story that showed how curiosity and accountability can coexist, and how collaboration accelerates adoption when technology and trust evolve side by side. Looking to the Second Half As we move into the second half of the year, the pace of change shows no sign of slowing. Agentic AI is no longer reserved for early adopters; it is rapidly becoming the new operational standard. The organisations that will lead the next phase are not simply those that spotted the trend early, but those building transparent, scalable, and responsible infrastructure to support it. At PubMatic, that mission shapes everything we do. We help partners adopt agentic AI with confidence, ensuring that automation amplifies human creativity rather than replacing it. We are proving every day that efficiency and transparency can strengthen one another, driving measurable value for buyers and publishers alike. We are not waiting for the future of agentic AI; we are already building and living it. One conversation, one campaign, and one trusted partnership at a time. And if the past six months are any indication, the acceleration we have seen from Milan to Madrid is only the beginning.

title: Anthropic: mayor acuerdo de derechos de autor en IA | Coderhouse
summary: Anthropic cerró el mayor acuerdo de derechos de autor de la historia de la IA. Qué establece y qué cambia para creadores, marcas y agencias.
body_text: Dan Patiño AI Strategy & Innovation en Coderhouse Inteligencia Artificial Anthropic cerró el mayor acuerdo de derechos de autor de la historia de la IA: qué cambia para creadores y marcas Publicado el 21 de julio de 2026 Anthropic, la empresa detrás del asistente de IA Claude, cerró el mayor acuerdo de derechos de autor de la historia de la inteligencia artificial: 1.500 millones de dólares para autores y editoriales. Un juez federal le dio la aprobación final este mes. Más allá del número, el caso deja lecciones concretas para cualquier marca o agencia que use IA para generar contenido. El acuerdo pone precio, por primera vez y a gran escala, al uso de material protegido para entrenar modelos de IA. Entender qué se resolvió y qué no ayuda a anticipar cómo va a quedar el terreno legal para todos los que trabajan con estas herramientas. Qué establece el acuerdo El pago de 1.500 millones de dólares se reparte entre autores y editoriales titulares de los derechos, con una compensación estimada de 3.000 dólares por obra, sobre alrededor de 500.000 trabajos. La demanda había sido impulsada por un grupo de autores que acusaba a la empresa de haber descargado libros desde bibliotecas piratas. Monto récord: es el mayor acuerdo conocido en un caso de derechos de autor en Estados Unidos. Compensación por obra: unos 3.000 dólares por cada libro incluido en el reclamo. Alcance amplio: la enorme mayoría de las obras cubiertas ya fueron reclamadas por sus titulares. El matiz clave: entrenamiento vs almacenamiento Acá está la lección más importante. En una etapa previa, el tribunal había señalado que entrenar un modelo con libros podía considerarse "uso legítimo" (fair use). Sin embargo, lo que sí constituyó una infracción fue mantener un repositorio de millones de libros obtenidos de fuentes piratas, más allá de si se usaron o no para entrenar. Dicho simple: el problema central no fue tanto aprender de los textos, sino cómo se consiguieron . La procedencia del material importa tanto como el uso que se le da. Qué cambia para creadores y marcas Si tu empresa o tu trabajo depende de herramientas de IA generativa, el fallo deja señales prácticas: La procedencia de los datos importa: conviene favorecer herramientas y proveedores que sean transparentes sobre con qué se entrenaron sus modelos. Los derechos de autor no desaparecen con la IA: generar contenido con estas herramientas no te exime de respetar la propiedad intelectual de terceros. Se viene más regulación: este acuerdo sienta un precedente que probablemente acelere marcos legales y licencias más claras. Oportunidad para autores: abre la puerta a modelos de licenciamiento donde los creadores cobren por el uso de sus obras. Para las marcas, la conclusión es tranquilizadora y exigente a la vez: la IA generativa sigue siendo una herramienta enorme, pero usarla de forma responsable —revisando fuentes, respetando derechos y documentando procesos— deja de ser opcional. Si querés aprovecharla bien, ayuda entender cómo se está aplicando en marketing y creación de contenido . La cobertura del caso ayuda a dimensionarlo: TechCrunch detalló los términos del acuerdo y The Next Web lo describió como el mayor de la historia del copyright , mientras que CNBC había reportado la aprobación preliminar . Cursos recomendados de Coderhouse Entender el contexto legal y técnico de la IA te permite usarla mejor y con menos riesgo. En Coderhouse podés hacerlo desde cualquier punto de partida: El Curso de Introducción a la Inteligencia Artificial te da el panorama completo, incluyendo el debate sobre datos y ética. El Curso de Creación de Contenido con IA te enseña a producir contenido de forma responsable y efectiva. Para perfiles de marketing, la Carrera de AI Marketing integra estrategia y uso profesional de estas herramientas. Formate para usar la IA con criterio: conocer las reglas del juego es parte de sacarle provecho. Preguntas frecuentes ¿Por qué Anthropic tuvo que pagar 1.500 millones de dólares? Por un acuerdo con autores y editoriales que la acusaban de haber usado libros obtenidos de bibliotecas piratas. El tribunal consideró que mantener ese repositorio de obras de origen ilícito constituía una infracción de derechos de autor, más allá del uso que se les diera. ¿El acuerdo significa que entrenar IA con libros es ilegal? No exactamente. En una etapa previa, el tribunal señaló que entrenar modelos con textos podía considerarse uso legítimo. Lo que se penalizó fue la forma de obtener y almacenar el material: descargarlo de fuentes piratas. La procedencia de los datos fue el punto clave. ¿Qué implica esto para quienes crean contenido con IA? Que los derechos de autor siguen vigentes. Usar herramientas de IA no exime de respetar la propiedad intelectual de terceros. Conviene elegir proveedores transparentes sobre sus datos de entrenamiento y documentar los procesos de creación. ¿Este caso va a cambiar la regulación de la IA? Muy probablemente. Al ser el mayor acuerdo de su tipo, sienta un precedente que puede acelerar marcos legales más claros y modelos de licenciamiento donde los creadores cobren por el uso de sus obras. Es un tema en plena evolución que conviene seguir de cerca. Sobre el autor Dan Patiño Soy Dan Patiño, responsable de AI Strategy & Innovation en Coderhouse. Mi día a día consiste en fusionar la gestión táctica del e-commerce (CRO, Email Marketing y SEO) con el desarrollo de soluciones disruptivas. Me especializo en crear apps internas con IA para automatizar tareas y potenciar la innovación dentro del equipo. Creo fielmente que la tecnología es el mejor aliado de la estrategia. Para profundizar en mi recorrido profesional, te espero en mi perfil de LinkedIn.

body_text: Flagright, the AI operating system for financial crime compliance, today announced that UniCredit in Poland uses Flagright to support transaction monitoring , customer screening , customer risk scoring , and case management across its digital banking operations.
